## Phase 3 Trial EFC14028 (COMET)

Study 1 (NCT02782741) was a randomized, double-blinded, multinational, multicenter trial comparing the efficacy and safety of NEXVIAZYME to alglucosidase alfa in 100 treatment-naive patients with LOPD.
The proposed dosage regimens have been tested in a phase 3 clinical trial in patients with LOPD (trial EFC14028) and a phase 2 clinical trial in patients with IOPD (trial ACT14132).

design.text: Randomized, double-blinded, multinational, multicenter, active-controlled trial comparing NEXVIAZYME to alglucosidase alfa; patients randomized 1:1 (stratified by baseline FVC, gender, age, and country) to 20 mg/kg every other week for 49 weeks, followed by an open-label long-term follow-up phase.

citations.quote: Study 1 (NCT02782741) was a randomized, double-blinded, multinational, multicenter trial comparing the efficacy and safety of NEXVIAZYME to alglucosidase alfa in 100 treatment-naive patients with LOPD. Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio based on baseline forced vital capacity (FVC), gender, age, and country to receive 20 mg/kg of NEXVIAZYME or alglucosidase alfa administered intravenously once every two weeks for 49 weeks. The trial included an open-label, long-term, follow-up phase of up to 5 years, in which patients in the alglucosidase alfa arm were switched to NEXVIAZYME treatment.

result.text: LS mean change in FVC (% predicted) at Week 49 was 2.9% (NEXVIAZYME) vs 0.5% (alglucosidase alfa); estimated treatment difference 2.4% (95% CI: -0.1, 5.0) favoring NEXVIAZYME, meeting pre-established noninferiority but not superiority. Key secondary endpoint 6MWT treatment difference was 30 meters (95% CI: 1.3 to 58.7).

citations.quote: At Week 49, the least squares (LS) mean change in FVC (% predicted) for patients treated with NEXVIAZYME and alglucosidase alfa was 2.9% and 0.5%, respectively. The estimated treatment difference was 2.4% (95% CI: -0.1, 5.0) favoring NEXVIAZYME (see Table 4).
** Noninferiority margin of 1.1% (p=0.0074). Statistical superiority of NEXVIAZYME over alglucosidase alfa was not achieved (p=0.06).

The estimated treatment difference in the distance walked in the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), a key secondary endpoint in EFC14028, was 30 meters (95% CI: 1.3 to 58.7), favoring avalglucosidase and supporting improved walking distance.

citations.quote: Nexviazyme (avalglucosidase alfa) is a modified recombinant human GAA intended for use as ERT in LOPD.

Avalglucosidase alfa is a second-generation ERT that provides an exogenous source of GAA and is a modification of alglucosidase alfa. While alglucosidase alfa has seven hexamannose structures, each containing two terminal mannose-6-phosphate (M6P) moieties conjugated to oxidized sialic acid residues, avalglucosidase alfa has a 15-fold increase in mannose-6-phosphate (M6P) moieties. key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions were hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis) and infusion-associated reactions. In Study 1 the most frequent AEs in NEXVIAZYME-treated patients (>5%) included headache (22%), fatigue (18%), diarrhea (12%), and nausea (12%); IARs occurred in 25% of NEXVIAZYME patients. Across the pooled safety population serious adverse events occurred in 25% (35/138) of patients.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (ARs) were hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis) and infusion-associated reactions, which presented most often as abdominal pain, arthralgia, back pain, chills, cough, diarrhea, dizziness, dyspnea, erythema, fatigue, headache, hypertension, musculoskeletal pain, myalgia, nausea, pain, pain in extremity, pruritus, pyrexia, rash, urticaria and vomiting.
IARs were reported in 13 (25%) of the NEXVIAZYME-treated patients.

Serious adverse events (SAEs) were reported in 25% (35/138) of patients treated with avalglucosidase alfa; SAEs reported in 2 or more patients included pneumonia, chills, pyrexia, respiratory distress, respiratory failure, and eyelid ptosis.

detail.text: Boxed warning for severe hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis), infusion-associated reactions, and risk of acute cardiorespiratory failure in susceptible patients. Patients have experienced life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis; discontinue immediately and initiate appropriate treatment if a severe reaction occurs.

citations.quote: ## **WARNING: SEVERE HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS, INFUSION-ASSOCIATED REACTIONS, and RISK OF ACUTE CARDIORESPIRATORY FAILURE IN SUSCEPTIBLE PATIENTS**

Patients treated with NEXVIAZYME have experienced life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis. Appropriate medical support measures, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation equipment, should be readily available during NEXVIAZYME administration.
